obtained.how: Wayback Machine capture (2015-09-18, openly downloadable) of the PDF that ASLO served free from its Limnology & Oceanography back-issue archive (aslo.org/lo/toc/vol_27/issue_5/0935.pdf); the journal's own scan

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the title page ('Limnol. Oceanogr., 27(5), 1982, 935-949')
bibliography.note: the third author prints as 'John D. Orcutt, Jr.'

claims.claim: Daphnia 'has no feeding threshold or reduced filtering activity at low concentrations' (cited as abstract only)
claims.location: p. 935 (PDF p. 1), Abstract; p. 945 (PDF p. 11), Discussion
claims.quote: Daphnia has no feeding threshold or reduced filtering activity at low concentrations
claims.conditions: laboratory, adult Daphnia magna (feeding runs: ten 2.7 ± 0.2-mm animals per replicate; behaviour: 2.6 ± 0.3-mm animals) on Chlamydomonas reinhardi at 0–10⁶ cells cm⁻³ (0–20 mg C L⁻¹), about 20 °C. Radiotracer ingestion cannot be measured much below 10³ cells cm⁻³ (20 µg C L⁻¹); the no-threshold conclusion rests on observed behaviour: filtering appendages beat at high constant rates below the incipient limiting concentration and all feeding movements continue in particle-free water (p. 945)
claims.note: The quotation is exact; the full text is now read, so '(abstract only)' can be dropped. The authors note that 'just looking at the data might suggest that filtering rate declines at 10³ cells·cm⁻³' (p. 944); the behaviour, not the ingestion data, settles it.

claims.claim: Daphnia clearance is type II down to zero food, with no threshold
claims.quote: the Ivlev model without a threshold, e.g. a Holling type 2 functional response curve
claims.conditions: as above; the Ivlev curve 'passes through the origin and plateaus at a maximum rate' (p. 944)

tried.note: CLOSED, no open copy listed (OpenAlex also lists none)

notes: Useful for the rewrite: hyperbolic and logarithmic fits to the same ingestion data imply a threshold near 9 × 10² cells cm⁻³ (p. 944), which the authors reject on behavioural grounds; respiration rose most around the incipient limiting concentration while ingestion rose three orders of magnitude (p. 945); Daphnia did not orient to algal patches (abstract). The finding is for one large species on one high-quality alga at 20 °C.
